item.title: St. Louis tornado recovery slowed by FEMA funding limits
item.description: Nearly a year after a powerful tornado ripped through north St. Louis, recovery efforts are now facing a major setback. FEMA will not cover most of the demolition costs for storm-damaged buildings.

item.title: Man charged with stealing Kate Chopin bust in Central West End
item.description: A man is in custody for stealing a $10,000 bust of a famed late 19th and early 20th century St. Louis-born writer last month.

item.title: Possible road rage shooting on I-70 leaves one injured
item.description: A person was shot in the arm during a possible road rage incident Thursday afternoon on Interstate 70 near Interstate 170, according to the Missouri State Highway Patrol.

item.title: Missouri sees improvement in water levels after dry spell
item.description: Missouri has picked up abundant rainfall over the last 48 hours, helping to restore some of the soil moisture lost during an exceptionally dry stretch.

item.title: Ballwin man accused of kidnapping, assaulting elderly woman
item.description: A Ballwin, Missouri, man is in custody for keeping an elderly woman locked in his home and routinely beating her.

item.title: Woman sentenced for having fiancé killed for insurance money
item.description: A St. Louis County woman appeared in federal court Thursday to be sentenced for orchestrating a murder-for-hire scheme to have her fiancé killed.

item.title: Several rescued from flooding at St. Francois State Park
item.description: At least six people were rescued by boat Thursday morning after floodwaters trapped multiple people inside St. Francois State Park, according to local fire officials.

item.title: Major remediation efforts continue along Coldwater Creek
item.description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is continuing its radioactive cleanup efforts in North St. Louis County along Coldwater Creek. New excavation work is scheduled to begin this month in the Cades Cove neighborhood.

item.title: Effort to raise speed limit in Missouri advances
item.description: The Missouri Senate approved a bill this week that would raise the state’s speed limit in rural areas from 70 to 75 miles per hour.

item.title: Parents call out summer camp safety gap
item.description: Parents are about to be inundated with summer camp possibilities, many of which are not licensed, not inspected, and not required to background check staff.
